name: Durrani Empire (Ahmad Shah Durrani)

areaKm2.note: Infobox: 2,000,000 km2 (undated; the whole empire with Punjab, Kashmir and Sindh) (high). Mid: the world_1783 Afghanistan polygon used as the border, about 1.15 million km2 on the sphere (Kandahar, Kabul, Herat, Balkh, Khorasan to Mashhad, Baluchistan); the 1783 file draws Punjab (Lahore), Multan and Sind as separate polygons. Low allows for the loose hold on Balkh and Khorasan.

population.note: Low: OWID Afghanistan 1760 = 2.87M (HYDE 3.3, modern borders, https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/population). Mid: that plus Iranian Khorasan and the Baluch and Pashtun lands inside the polygon (educated estimate of about 1.5M from OWID Iran 1760 = 5.79M and Pakistan 1760 = 15.2M). High: infobox 14 million for the whole empire with its Indian provinces (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire). The phase-3 formula gave 47 million for this polygon, far too high.

urbanization.note: Educated guess: caravan cities Kandahar, Kabul, Herat and Mashhad in a pastoral and oasis-farming country.

activePersonnel.note: Panipat field army (14 January 1761): 41,800 Afghan cavalry, 28,000 of them regular, plus 2,000 camel-gun troops in the reserve (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_Battle_of_Panipat); the 32,000 Rohilla infantry and Shuja-ud-Daula's 3,000 men and 50-60 guns were allies and are not counted. Mid adds a few thousand for garrisons of Kandahar, Kabul, Herat and Lahore. Low: the 28,000 regulars plus the 10,000 ghulam core (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire) overlap, so about 30,000.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: Pashtun, Baluch, Uzbek and Qizilbash tribal contingents callable for a campaign but not under arms.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess: gunners, camel and baggage men of the royal army.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: Mughal Empire 1690 and Maratha 1760 snapshots (Barua 2005 p. 47 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_of_the_Mughal_Empire: about 3% of the population were armed men). A tribal society where most men bore arms could reach more; kept at the analogy.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: 19,000 mailed Afghan horsemen under Shah Wali Khan at Panipat (mid); 28,000 regular cavalry (infobox) (high); low = the 10,000 mounted ghulams of the royal guard (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mail, lance, broadsword and blunderbuss (sher-bacha ghulams); good horses.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: long-service ghulams, a third of them former Qizilbash of Nader Shah's army.

count.note: 41,800 Afghan cavalry less the 19,000 mailed horse = 22,800, including the 2,000 camel-mounted zamburak and shutarnal gunners of the reserve (mid). Low: 41,800 less the 28,000 regulars = 13,800 irregulars. High allows for tribal horse outside the battle line.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: tribal lance and sword cavalry with some matchlocks; camel swivel guns.

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: experienced raiders of five invasions of India since 1748.

count.note: Educated guess: tribal jezail infantry and fort garrisons; infantry played a very small role in the Durrani army (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire).

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: tribal levies.

count.note: Educated guess. Artillery played a very small role apart from camel-mounted swivel guns (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire); the 2,000 zamburaks are counted as light cavalry, not as pieces. The 50-60 guns at Panipat belonged to the ally Shuja-ud-Daula.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: few, light pieces; outranged by the Maratha French-made guns at Panipat.

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.75 (proven commanders). Evidence: Ahmad Shah, trained under Nader Shah, blockaded the Maratha camp until hunger forced it out and committed his reserve at the decisive moment at Panipat.

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: ghulam core with tribal contingents loyal to the shah's success and plunder.

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75 minus. Evidence: recent victories in India; troops wanted to return home with their plunder, which ended the campaign in 1761.

weapons.note: Anchor: 5 (1600, arquebus/musket, field cannon). Evidence: lance, sword, matchlocks, blunderbusses and camel swivel guns; little field artillery.

armor.note: Anchor: 4-5. Evidence: mail for the regular horse.

ships.note: Anchor: 0-1. Evidence: landlocked; ferries and boats on the Indus only.

fortification.note: Anchor: 4-5. Evidence: walled Kandahar (new city founded by Ahmad Shah), Bala Hisar of Kabul, Herat citadel.

logistics.note: Anchor: 4-5. Evidence: camel and horse transport, foraging and plunder; cut the Maratha supply lines at Panipat while keeping his own open via Rohilkhand.

isr.note: Anchor: 5 minus. Evidence: light-cavalry patrols that intercepted Maratha supply convoys.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/gdp-per-capita-maddison-project-database.csv?v=1&csvType=full&useColumnShortNames=true) has no Afghanistan value before 1950 (1,156, high). Analogues: India 1750 = 1,068, Iran 1820 = 877 (low side). 2011 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. A conquest state financed by Indian tribute and plunder; the share of domestic output is not documented.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: crafts of the caravan cities (textiles, carpets, arms) in a pastoral and oasis economy.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Irrigated oases and herding; the Indian provinces (outside the border) were the grain surplus.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the other pre-modern snapshots.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: caravan routes and passes, almost no engineered road.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: landlocked inside the border polygon (Sind and the Makran ports lay outside).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Cavalry armies that campaigned 1,000 km from Kandahar to Delhi, living off the land and tribute.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: camels, horses and pack animals of a pastoral country (about 10% of the population); no count found.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3 row (the rubric names Afghanistan): mountains, deep strategic depth, harsh climate and an armed tribal population.

notes: Snapshot = January 1761, Ahmad Shah's army at the Third Battle of Panipat. Personnel: the royal army and the tribal cavalry in the field are activePersonnel; the Rohilla and Awadh allies at Panipat are separate states and not counted; uncalled tribal contingents are trainedReserves. Territory and population = the world_1783 Afghanistan polygon (Afghanistan, Khorasan, Baluchistan); Punjab, Kashmir, Multan and Sind were held or tributary in 1761 but are outside the border and the population, and includes is empty. Weakest values: population mid (composite), artillery, and the economy and logistics guesses; Maddison has no series for the region before 1950. Doctrine archetype-steppe-nomad: a cavalry army of raids, blockade and mounted firepower rather than a linear gunpowder army.
